transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date/Time: 2025-07-15 16:00 PDT
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Solstice - Dir ML), Tom Nguyen (Solstice - CTO), Priya Rao (Solstice - PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Solstice is evaluating open model variants across hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments. Priority: multilingual customer support (EN/ES/FR/DE/JP), long-context for session history (>=64k tokens desired for long receipts / shopping sessions), and tool-calling to product catalog and order APIs. Concerns: data residency, SOC2, latency targets (p95 < 300ms for chat), cost. Next: Redwood to share SOC2 summary and sandbox for benchmarking; schedule SE deep-dive.

Topics: model families, context length, quantization/latency tradeoffs, multilingual quality, tool/function-calling, deployment modes, security/compliance, benchmark plan.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, happy Tuesday. Thanks for carving out time. Quick intros and then Samir will jump into technical questions.
[00:00:08] Tom (Solstice): Hi all, Tom here. We've got Lena who runs the ML team and Priya on PM — we'll be focused on model selection and integration constraints.
[00:00:15] Lena (Solstice): Morning, thanks. We're evaluating options because our in-chat and voice assistants need better long-term context — shopping carts, returns, and multi-turn browsing across sessions.
[00:00:24] Maya: Great, that's exactly what we want to scope. Samir, you wanna kick off on model families and context?
[00:00:29] Samir (Redwood SE): Sure. Quick note: I'll use shorthand — when I say "open models" I mean the LLaMA-derivatives, Mistral-style, and a few opt-like families. We support running these on Hosted, Dedicated pools, or Private (VPC/on-prem). Can you share your latency and throughput targets?
[00:00:48] Priya (Solstice): For chat we target p95 <= 300ms for text-only completions; for multimodal/large prompts we'd accept up to 700ms. Throughput initially modest — 50 concurrent sessions but peaks up to 500 during promos.
[00:01:03] Samir: Okay, good. For p95 <300ms you generally need smaller quantized variants or a high-throughput Dedicated pool. Hosted can hit those numbers for smaller models or with optimistic routing but cost can ramp with concurrent sessions.
[00:01:18] Lena: We also need long context: some workflows want 64k tokens, others 8k is enough. Is that realistic on your platform?
[00:01:26] Samir: Yes — we support models with extended context. There are tradeoffs: large context models need more memory and increase per-token compute. For example, the open-64k style models or context-extended LlamaX variants run well on Dedicated or Private with GPUs that have larger memory — A100 80GB or 600GB VM class. On Hosted we have selective models that support 32k-64k but we advise Dedicated for consistent SLOs at that scale.
[00:01:50] Maya: Also worth noting we have prefix/KV caching and session stitching to reduce repeated compute for long histories — that's Redwood's automatic caching, though it behaves differently by deployment mode.
[00:02:01] Tom: Explain the caching bit — will it split the session or we always re-send full history?
[00:02:05] Samir: Good question. You can send deltas; we maintain KV cache server-side for the session ID which avoids re-encoding earlier tokens. On Private, customers can control TTLs and encryption. On Hosted, we keep a short-lived cache with configurable retention — but if you need retention for days for business logic, Private or Dedicated with persistent KV cache is better.
[00:02:25] Priya: Multilingual: we need top-tier ES and FR, decent DE and JP. Do open models perform there or do we need a specialized model?
[00:02:33] Samir: Open models vary. Mistral-derivative and some LLaMA-3 forks have relatively solid multilingual hits, but they can be weaker on Japanese. We often recommend a multilingual base model and a smaller fine-tuned adapter for important locales. For Hosted, we have curated models with measured multilingual perf — we can share benchmark sheets.
[00:02:51] Lena: Do you support on-the-fly model routing? Like route Spanish queries to a Spanish-optimized model?
[00:02:57] Samir: Yes — routing policies can be per-tenant or per-route. You can set locale heuristics to pick a model or fallback chain. That works across Hosted/Dedicated/Private though the pool configuration differs.
[00:03:09] Tom: Tool-calling — our catalog and order APIs need to be callable. We looked into OpenAI function calling. How does Redwood support that?
[00:03:16] Maya: We support function/tool calling with structured outputs; the SEs can demo our function-calling flow. We also support streaming responses while invoking tools so you can interleave a generated response with API calls.
[00:03:27] Samir: Implementation note: we provide a tool schema layer that maps to your APIs. On Hosted, schemas are stored in the control plane with RBAC; on Private the control plane can be customer-managed. We also surface tool logs in the Console for tracing.
[00:03:40] Lena: Any limits or gotchas — like synchronous vs async tools, or security around credentials?
[00:03:45] Samir: Tool calls can be sync or async. For sensitive credentials we integrate with KMS/HSM and support per-tool service accounts. On Private deployments customers can bring their own KMS. We'll capture in the security doc I'll send.
[00:03:58] Priya: About data residency and compliance — we are EU-first for a chunk of customers. We need SOC2 and data-at-rest encryption and logging for audits.
[00:04:06] Maya: We have SOC2 plus optional audits for enterprise. Private deployments give you full control of data residency. For Hosted we have region pinning and data handling agreements; we can share the SOC2 summary and details for encryption and log retention.
[00:04:18] Tom: Cost — what drives cost most? Is context length a killer?
[00:04:22] Samir: Context length, model size, and request rate. Caching and batching reduce unit cost. Quantization helps a lot on Dedicated/Private. Also model choice: LLMs with 7-13B parameter quantized variants are usually an order of magnitude cheaper than large 70B models while often being sufficient for many tasks.
[00:04:40] Lena: For our SLAs, sometimes we prefer Dedicated so we know we won't be bumped during big campaigns. Is Dedicated reserved capacity or dynamic?
[00:04:46] Maya: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with configurable autoscaling and burst capacity. You get SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. It's designed for predictable throughput.
[00:04:55] Tom: Private — we'd need VPC and on-prem options for the most sensitive B2B customers. How intrusive is the private install?
[00:05:02] Samir: There's a few flavors: VPC-hosted private control plane where we still orchestrate but network is customer managed; and on-prem package for air-gapped environments. On-prem requires a small infra footprint — orchestrator + model servers — and we provide installation docs. We also support HSM integration for key management.
[00:05:18] Priya: Any experience with custom fine-tuning or RLHF for retail domain?
[00:05:22] Samir: We recommend adapters or fine-tuning for catalog glossaries and pricing tone. For quality-sensitive cases we do data-primed fine-tunes. Redwood also offers eval hooks to monitor regressions after model rollouts.
[00:05:34] Lena: Can we run scoring on embeddings for semantic search across product descriptions and reviews?
[00:05:38] Samir: Yes — embeddings are supported; we provide per-embedding cost metrics. For scale, we suggest an embeddings pipeline with shardable vector DBs; we can show throughput numbers in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[00:05:48] Tom: Benchmarks — we want to run our top-100 prompt set across EN/ES/JP, and long-history sessions. Will Redwood run these or we do it?
[00:05:56] Maya: We can provide a sandbox token + recommended runner. Typically we provision a short sandbox with credits and a benchmark sheet; your team uploads prompts and we run both hosted and dedicated configurations and return a summary. Samir: I'll set that up.
[00:06:08] Priya: Regarding latency for 64k contexts, do you have any real numbers?
[00:06:12] Samir: On a Dedicated A100-80GB with a 64k-capable model and quantized kernels, we see generation latency in the 300-600ms range for mid-length outputs (50-150 tokens) depending on batch. But that assumes efficient KV cache use and batch tuning. Hosted numbers vary and are less predictable under noisy multi-tenant load.
[00:06:28] Maya: Also note streaming adds small overhead but improves perceived latency; function calls add round-trip time for external APIs.
[00:06:35] Lena: For model governance, can we pin model versions and do canary rollouts?
[00:06:40] Samir: Yes — Console supports version pinning, canary splits, and A/B rollouts. You can define fallback chains if a model regresses. We also tie rollouts to eval suites so you can block if metrics drop.
[00:06:52] Priya: Any recommended models for retail multilingual + tools?
[00:06:56] Samir: A common pattern: base multilingual ~13B quantized as the primary model, with locale adapters or smaller specialised models for JP. For tool-calling, ensure the model's parsing reliability is high; we have a curated set we call "tool-friendly" models. I'll put names in the follow-up sheet —sorry I might mangle some model names in the call — e.g., the Llama3-extended, Mistral-x-64k, and a few derivatives.
[00:07:16] Tom: Great. On security again — we need audit logs for tool calls and data access for at least 1 year. Is that standard?
[00:07:22] Maya: Audit logs are an add-on in Hosted but bundled for Dedicated/Private enterprise tiers. Retention periods are configurable. We'll include that in the pricing/options deck.
[00:07:33] Priya: Any pitfalls around tokenization for multilingual: do you recompute token counts differently?
[00:07:38] Samir: Tokenization differences do impact cost; languages like JP or CJK can have different token rates. We include tokenization estimates in the benchmark so you can estimate TCO per locale.
[00:07:49] Lena: For observability, can we get per-request token-level cost breakdowns?
[00:07:53] Samir: Yes — Console provides token-level cost, latency breakdowns, and per-route dashboards. We also provide tracing hooks for distributed tracing if you want to link application traces to inference requests.
[00:08:05] Maya: Quick note — pricing: hosted is pay-as-you-go; Dedicated is reserved commit with discounts; Private is license + infra. Our pricing sheet will show example math for the configurations you described.
[00:08:16] Tom: Ok sounds good. A few random clarifications: 1) Does Redwood do model quantization for us or we do it? 2) How do you handle model updates and security patches?
[00:08:26] Samir: 1) We handle quantization tooling on Dedicated/Hosted. For Private, we can provide tooling and help. 2) Model updates are managed by you for private on-prem; for Hosted/Dedicated we provide model rollout channels and security patch notes.
[00:08:38] Priya: Could we get a short POC: hosted small model vs dedicated quantized 13B; run the top-100 prompt set in EN/ES, and run a 10-session 64k-history scenario?
[00:08:48] Maya: Absolutely. Typical POC runbook: we provision sandbox, you upload prompts + sample sessions, we run hosted vs dedicated and return latency/cost/quality metrics. We'll also include transcripts of function-calling flows.
[00:08:59] Tom: Any specific infra hints from your side to prepare?
[00:09:03] Samir: Provide sample payload sizes, expected concurrency profile, and specific API schemas for tool calls. Also share where you want the data to live (region). Lena: We'll share top-500 SKUs and sample chat logs but will obfuscate PII.
[00:09:17] Maya: Great. I'll follow up with an options deck and SOC2 summary. Samir will send sandbox access and the benchmark sheet. Let's schedule the SE-deep-dive for next week with your infra and security folks.
[00:09:29] Priya: That works for us. One last note — we have some internal latency budget for voice (ASR + model) which is tight; may need edge routing or region placement.
[00:09:37] Samir: We can explore colocated inferencing or region placement. For voice you might want lower-latency GPU families or embeddings on a separate fast path. We'll surface options in the follow-up.
[00:09:48] Tom: Thanks everyone. That's a wrap for us.
[00:09:51] Maya: Thanks all — follow-ups coming.

(Transcript ends, auto-timestamps approximate; occasional transcription mis-hearings: "KV cash" for KV cache, "Llama three" or "Mistraal" typos present.)
